subject: Proposal: 3yr flexible reserve + credit-smoothing for Dedicated GPU pool

Subject: Proposal: 3yr flexible reserve + credit-smoothing for Dedicated GPU pool

Hi Emma — attaching our updated commercial for the Dedicated GPU pool. Key changes based on last week's call: 1) a flexible "credit-smoothing" option that lets Peregrine shift unused quarterly credits forward up to two quarters, 2) a stair-step term discount ladder tied to year-over-year committed TPU-hours (10% Y1 prepay baseline, +2% if Y2 commit >= Y1*1.10, +1% more if Y3 commit >= Y2*1.10), and 3) a phased ramp schedule that treats Q1 as a partial onboarding tranche to avoid front-loading credit burn.

Summary (see attached redwood_flex_ramp_proposal_v3.pdf):
- 36-month term with annual prepay by invoice
- Year 1: four quarterly tranches (30% / 25% / 25% / 20%) by committed TPU-equivalent; optional smoothing pool
- Canary capacity: 2 GPU equivalents kept outside committed pool for 60 days during ramp
- Underutilization treatment: unused quarterly credits can be carried forward (max 2 quarters) or converted to account credit at 60% face value at annual reconciliation
- Early termination: standard termination formula but we can cap exposure in year 1 to 3 months of committed spend if output quality thresholds are met

Ask: can your procurement team confirm whether Q1 partial tranche (30%) plus carry-forward would meet your budgeting constraints? If yes, I'd like to book 30 minutes to walk through the attached pricing_redline.xlsx and the revised SOW.

Attachments: redwood_flex_ramp_proposal_v3.pdf, pricing_redline.xlsx

Best,

Subject: Re: Proposal: 3yr flexible reserve + credit-smoothing for Dedicated GPU pool

Emma — quick answers inline below. Quoted your questions for context.

> Can unused credits be reallocated across regions (we have a small EMEA cluster)?
Yes — credits are regional by default but we can enable a global smoothing pool that allows credits to be applied across regions up to 20% of the quarterly pool (to protect capacity alignment). We'd include a short addendum in the SOW specifying regional redistribution limits.

> What happens if our sustained run rate in Y2 is lower than the commit trigger for the extra 2% discount? Is there a pro-rata protection?
We require a signed increase commit to lock the additional 2% (it's applied once the signed year-2 commitment is >= 110% of year-1). If during reconciliation the actual usage falls below the signed commit, the reconciliation will revert the extra 2% on the delta and a small true-up will be invoiced or applied as an account credit (we typically true-up at 60% recovery on unused credits). We can add a carve-out for force-majeure/major outages.

> Penalties: the attachment mentions an "early termination formula" — can you confirm the capped exposure in written terms?
We can cap year-1 early termination exposure to the equivalent of three months of committed monthly spend. Year-2/3 follow the standard amortization schedule in the proposal.

I've attached pricing_redline.xlsx with inline notes on the discount ladder and an expanded reconciliation example. I've also looped Lauren and Marcus to coordinate onboarding credits / finance approvals.

Propose a 30-min call Monday 2026-05-04 at 10:00 PDT to walk through the SOW and DocuSign flow — does that time work?

Best,
Priyom

Appreciate the quick responses. Procurement provided a counter-proposal on the ramp split: they want a softer Q1 to avoid hitting our cash flow target, proposing 20% / 25% / 30% / 25% for Y1. They also asked for the onboarding credit to be applied as a bill credit rather than contra-revenue (simpler for our accounting). Finally, they want a capped early termination exposure at 2 months if we hit a 95% availability SLA during the first 6 months.

I'm attaching our procurement questionnaire for SOC2 and compliance items. If Redwood can accept the Q1 softer tranche and apply the onboarding credit as a bill credit, we can move to signature quickly.

Emma
